title: Tiger Family — AI upsizing
subtitle: An adult tigress and her cub at Bandhavgarh tiger reserve, India, on a forest path at sunset. Captured at ISO 1250 on the OM-1 at 75 mm (150 mm equivalent), 1/640s f/4.5.
editor_note: All of the AI upsampling ran on the full 5184 px source image (shown above for context). For AI analysis and on-page display we worked with a 1928 px crop around the adult tiger taken from each 1× / 2× / 4× output — the full-resolution 4× upsamples were too large for darwain's evaluation pipeline and impractical to display at native scale.
exif_summary: OM-1 with OM 40-150mm F2.8 at 75mm (150mm equivalent), 1/640s at f/4.5, ISO 1250

images.title: Original 1x image cropped sample
images.caption: Processed with DxO RAW and basic tone and color adjustments, cropped to a sample of the original image.

critique.text: The original cropped sample shows good base detail and natural rendering, serving as a solid starting point. Comparing the upscaling methods overall: Topaz Gigapixel clearly outperforms the others by successfully generating realistic fine details (like fur and leaf textures), making the image look truly higher resolution. ON1 Resize tends to produce a somewhat 'painted' effect, losing finer textures while sharpening edges. Lightroom's Super Resolution yields a softer result, lacking the crispness of the Topaz output but avoiding the artificial look of ON1.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 2x
images.caption: Upscaled with Gigapixel v1.1.3. 5184x3456 => 10368x6912 (2x) Model: High Fidelity V2, denoise: 0.58, sharpen: 0.39, decompression: 0.01

critique.text: This is arguably the best result among the upscaled versions. The 2x upscale with Topaz Gigapixel High Fidelity model produces excellent, crisp details that look highly natural. The fur texture is beautifully preserved and enhanced, and the background elements remain distinct without looking over-processed. It hits the sweet spot of increasing resolution while maintaining photographic integrity.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 4x
images.caption: Upsized 4x using Topal GigaPixel High Fidelity

critique.text: Topaz Gigapixel has done a remarkable job at 4x upscaling. It has managed to generate convincing fine detail in the tiger's fur, the bark of the trees, and the surrounding foliage. While a very close inspection might reveal slight artifacts typical of AI upscaling, the overall impression is much crisper and more realistic than the ON1 attempts, maintaining a good balance between sharpness and natural texture.

images.title: Lightroom Super Resolution 2x
images.caption: Lightroom Super Resolution 2x, applied to high quality jpeg of the cropped sample

critique.text: Upscaling a JPEG with Lightroom Super Resolution has yielded a relatively soft result. It avoids the painterly artifacts of ON1 but fails to introduce the crisp, convincing fine details seen in the Topaz Gigapixel versions. It essentially looks like a slightly softer version of the original, not fully capitalizing on the potential of AI upscaling, likely hindered by starting from a compressed JPEG rather than the RAW file.

images.title: ON1 Resize 2x
images.caption: Upsized with ON1 Resize 2x, best quality. Used Sharpening for screen with default options.

critique.text: Similar characteristics to the 4x version, but slightly less pronounced due to the smaller scaling factor. It still exhibits a slightly unnatural, processed look with somewhat flattened textures in the fur compared to the more successful upscaling methods. The sharpening for screen has made the edges contrasty but hasn't fully preserved the organic feel of the original.

images.title: ON1 Resize 4x
images.caption: Upsized with ON1 Resize 4x, best quality. Used Sharpening for screen with default options.

critique.text: The 4x upscaling by ON1 Resize has resulted in a slightly artificial, almost painterly look. While the edges of the tiger stripes are relatively sharp, the finer details like individual hairs in the fur and the textures of the leaves and ground appear somewhat smudged or lost. The applied sharpening seems to have emphasized larger structures rather than recovering micro-contrast.
